dimensions.label: Terrain
dimensions.how: Median slope, roughness and relief of a 32 km window on a common 450 m grid, compared on log scales (a factor of 20 apart scores 0).

dimensions.label: Thermal
dimensions.how: Mean and peak surface temperature in kelvin, compared directly: 150 K apart scores 0. For the lava-tube target, cave sites are compared on cave-interior temperature.

dimensions.label: Water and ice
dimensions.how: Dryness (log of annual precipitation), column water vapour (log scale) and ground-ice class, in equal parts.

dimensions.label: Geology
dimensions.how: Weighted overlap (Jaccard) of surface materials and landforms on a fixed 17-term vocabulary, coded from the cited papers.

dimensions.label: Dust and wind
dimensions.how: Dust optical depth compared directly (1.0 apart scores 0) and wind dynamic pressure ½ρv² on a log scale, so thin Martian air counts.

dimensions.label: Sterility
dimensions.how: One minus vegetation cover from growing-season MODIS NDVI (0.08 = bare, 0.68 = full canopy). The targets have none.

dimensions.label: Sun angle
dimensions.how: Highest solar elevation of the year from latitude and axial tilt; 90° apart scores 0.

targets.name: Connecting Ridge
targets.rationale: The ridge between Shackleton and de Gerlache craters is one of the Artemis III candidate regions: near-continuous grazing sunlight for power, minutes away from permanently shadowed craters that trap water ice.

notes.text: A site on the Shackleton rim is sunlit continuously for about 240 days a year; its longest total darkness is about 1.5 days.
Only about 3.5% of polar cold traps show ice at the surface; some pixels may hold about 30 wt% ice mixed with regolith.

facts.label: Ground with yearly maximum below 110 K (cold traps)
Ground where ice is stable in the top metre or so
Hottest ground in the window (sun-facing slope)
Coldest yearly-average ground in the window

targets.name: Mare Tranquillitatis pit
targets.rationale: A collapse pit about 100 m across and 105 m deep in mare basalt. Its shadowed floor holds near 290 K around the clock, and any cave beyond it would shield a habitat from radiation, micrometeorites and the 300 K swing of the surface.

notes.text: Permanently shadowed parts of the pit stay near 290 K; the sunlit floor can exceed 420 K.
The open surface around it swings from about 95 K before dawn to 387–397 K at noon.

targets.name: Jezero Crater
targets.rationale: Perseverance's landing site: a 45 km crater that held a lake, with a preserved delta, olivine-rich floor units and marginal carbonates. The reference site for biosignature search and sample return.

targets.name: Arcadia Planitia
targets.rationale: Smooth northern plains over a decametres-thick sheet of excess water ice, shallow enough to reach with a drill: the leading resource case for a crewed Mars landing site.

notes.text: Radar and terraced craters indicate a widespread, decametres-thick layer of excess ice, about 10⁴ km³.

sites.name: Yungay, Atacama Desert
sites.summary: Hyper-arid core of the Atacama: salt-cemented soils with almost no organics.
sites.use: Life-detection instrument tests at the dry limit of microbial life; drill and sample-handling trials in salt-cemented soil.

sites.name: Haughton crater, Devon Island
sites.summary: A 23 km impact structure in polar desert with continuous permafrost.
sites.use: Crewed traverse and EVA operations, impact-hydrothermal biosignature studies, drilling into permafrost.

sites.name: University Valley, McMurdo Dry Valleys
sites.summary: Coldest, driest ice-free ground on Earth: dry permafrost over ice-cemented soil.
sites.use: Ice-table drilling (the Phoenix and IceBreaker case), cold-limit habitability, polygon mapping.

sites.name: Askja, central highlands
sites.summary: Barren basaltic sand and lava around an active caldera; an Apollo training ground.
sites.use: Rover and sampling tests on basaltic sand and glass; alteration mineralogy for orbital spectra.

sites.name: Mauna Kea summit region
sites.summary: High, dry volcanic summit with palagonitic tephra close to Mars dust in spectra.
sites.use: Regolith simulant source, resource-extraction and rover field tests on tephra.

sites.name: Corona lava tube, Lanzarote
sites.summary: An 8 km lava tube with skylights in a dry volcanic island; used for astronaut geology training.
sites.use: Cave mapping, skylight descent and communications trials for tube exploration.

sites.name: Río Tinto headwaters
sites.summary: Acid, iron-rich river system precipitating sulfates and iron oxides.
sites.use: Biosignature preservation in iron sulfates and oxides; subsurface drilling for chemolithotrophs.

sites.name: Lake Salda shore
sites.summary: Alkaline lake in ultramafic rock with Mg-carbonate microbialites and deltas.
sites.use: The closest mineral match to Jezero's marginal carbonates: where to look for biosignatures in a carbonate shoreline.

sites.name: Dallol, Danakil Depression
sites.summary: Hydrothermal salt dome below sea level: hot, hyper-acid, hyper-saline brines.
sites.use: Testing the limits of habitability and the risk of false-positive biosignatures in salt and iron minerals.

sites.name: Kaluts, Lut Desert
sites.summary: Mega-yardang field holding the highest satellite land-surface temperatures on Earth.
sites.use: Rover mobility across yardangs and wind-scoured hardpan; thermal stress tests for hardware.

sites.name: Lonar crater
sites.summary: One of very few fresh impact craters in basalt, holding an alkaline lake.
sites.use: Ejecta and shocked-basalt sampling strategy for craters in mare and Martian lava plains.

sites.name: Dalangtan, Qaidam Basin
sites.summary: High, cold, hyper-arid basin of evaporites, yardangs and polygonal salt crust.
sites.use: Evaporite biosignature search; mobility on salt polygons and yardangs; cold-arid operations.

sites.name: Salar de Uyuni, Altiplano
sites.summary: The largest salt flat on Earth, at 3,650 m under intense ultraviolet light.
sites.use: Navigation and autonomy on featureless terrain; brine and salt resources; high-UV instrument tests.

sites.name: North Pole Dome, Pilbara
sites.summary: 3.5-billion-year-old volcanic and hot-spring rocks holding some of Earth's oldest fossils.
sites.use: Training ground for recognising ancient biosignatures in altered basalt, as at Jezero.

sites.name: Kazumura Cave, Kīlauea
sites.summary: The longest known lava tube on Earth, about 65 km, under rainforest.
sites.use: Long-range robotic traverses and mapping inside a tube.

sites.name: Undara lava tubes
sites.summary: A 160 km lava flow with a chain of large tubes and roof collapses in dry savanna.
sites.use: Collapse-pit entry and tube-scale survey; tube widths approach those inferred for Mars.

sites.name: Umm Jirsan, Harrat Khaybar
sites.summary: A 1.5 km lava tube with collapse entrances in a bare desert lava field.
sites.use: Skylight descent and habitat siting in a tube whose surroundings are as barren as the cave.

sites.name: Emi Koussi, Tibesti
sites.summary: Saharan shield volcano with nested calderas, compared with Elysium Mons since Mariner 9.
sites.use: Orbital-to-ground validation for volcanic landforms; remote, unvegetated traverse planning.

sites.name: Tolbachik scoria fields, Kamchatka
sites.summary: Fresh basaltic cinder plain from the 1975 eruption, with permafrost on the volcanoes above.
sites.use: Wheel and excavation tests in loose basaltic cinder; cold volcanic terrain operations.

sites.name: Pali Aike volcanic field
sites.summary: Cold, wind-blasted basaltic plain of maars and cones in southern Patagonia.
sites.use: Wind-load and dust tests for surface hardware; maar and cone geology traverses.

sites.name: Mistastin (Kamestastin) crater rim
sites.summary: A 28 km impact crater in anorthosite, the rock of the lunar highlands.
sites.use: Sampling impact melt in anorthosite, the closest rock match to the lunar south pole.

sites.name: Ibyuk pingo, Tuktoyaktuk
sites.summary: Ice-cored hills and massive ground ice in Arctic coastal lowland.
sites.use: Ground-ice detection by radar and drilling; ice mining trials under a thin dry cover.

sites.name: Batagaika megaslump, Yakutia
sites.summary: An 80 m deep thaw scar exposing a thick ice sheet in section.
sites.use: A scarp of exposed buried ice, like those imaged on Mars: stratigraphy and sampling of an ice cliff.

sites.name: Tso Kar basin, Ladakh
sites.summary: Cold, dry salt-lake basin at 4,500 m with hot springs nearby.
sites.use: High-altitude human operations; evaporite and hot-spring biosignature targets.

sites.name: Tenoumer crater
sites.summary: A sharp 1.9 km simple crater in the western Sahara.
sites.use: Crater-rim traverse and ejecta sampling on a small, fresh, bare crater.

sites.name: Ward Hunt Island
sites.summary: Northernmost land in Canada: polar desert with months of low sun and of darkness.
sites.use: Power and thermal design for long nights and grazing sunlight; isolated crew operations.

sites.name: Namib Sand Sea, Sossusvlei
sites.summary: Large linear and star dunes of iron-coated sand in a coastal desert.
sites.use: Dune mobility and sand-transport studies for Martian dune fields.
